standard_prerequisites: Homotopies between endofunctions of A and the action of a function on paths (ap), with its definitional behaviour on reflexivity.
Path concatenation and inversion with the unit laws and associativity of concatenation.
core_obligations: Prove, for a homotopy H from an endofunction f to itself and every x in A, the identification H(f(x)) equals ap of f applied to H(x).
Carry out the whiskering cancellation using the naturality square of H.
proof_roadmap: Draw the naturality square: by naturality of H (the retained context), the paths ap of f applied to H(x) concatenated with H(x) and H(f(x)) concatenated with H(x) are identified.
Whisker the identification on the right by the inverse of H(x) to cancel the common factor H(x).

Re-associate the resulting concatenations (the author notes the associativity paths are suppressed; these are instances of the associativity law for concatenation) and conclude H(f(x)) equals ap of f applied to H(x).
difficulty_reason: A whiskering-and-cancellation argument over a commutative square; the steps are short but require careful bookkeeping of concatenation algebra, part of which the author suppresses as standard re-association.
